title: Varied extent children are measured at intrinsic size
evidence: Flutter places item 3 at rect [0,111,800,162] (size [800,51]) and materializes items 0-2. Incular reports item 3 at [0,0,800,0] and items 0-2 absent, unchanged on all three frames. Revalidated at a19bf487.
impact: A SliverVariedExtentList whose children rely on itemExtentBuilder for main-axis size collapses to zero and disappears, shifting following slivers and corrupting scroll extent.
cause: VariableExtentRenderSliver builds each child with sliver_child_constraints(..., None), leaving the main axis unbounded; the callback extent is used only as an index estimate, and the measured size is recorded afterwards.
fix_direction: Pass each materialized item's callback extent as a tight main-axis constraint, matching Flutter's fixed-extent adaptor.
limitations: Only the zero-height case with dimensionless children was observed.

title: Floating headers omit Flutter's default scroll-end snap
evidence: Both controllers end at offset 60. At frame 5 Flutter's header is at [0,-60,800,10] and animates fully into view (rect [0,0,800,70] by frame 24). Incular stays at [0,-30,800,40] through the final frame. Revalidated at a19bf487.
impact: With Incular's default floating header a partly visible header can remain stranded after scrolling stops, while Flutter settles it to an edge.
cause: SliverFloatingHeader.snap defaults to false and the scroll-activity subscription is created only when it is enabled. Flutter always performs the partial-header end animation; snapMode selects the layout mode, not whether snapping happens.
fix_direction: Match Flutter's default end snap; keep snap presentation modes independent of the enable switch, with an explicit opt-out only if the Incular API needs one.
limitations: Only the wheel-scroll path is tested. Touch-drag settling, snapMode.scroll and custom durations are unchecked.

title: SliverFillRemaining without a scroll body keeps its largest past extent
evidence: Phase 0 has a 45 px adapter above a hasScrollBody:false fill; phase 1 grows the adapter to 200 px. Flutter's fill settles at 400 px (rect ending 600). Incular's fill stays at 555 px (rect ending 755) on the last two frames; size [800,555] vs [800,400], max diff 155 px.
impact: Content above a SliverFillRemaining(hasScrollBody: false) that grows leaves the fill too large, so the scroll extent is wrong and the fill overflows the viewport. Common in empty-state layouts beside a changing header.
cause: FillRemainingRenderSliver computes extent as self.extent.get().max(remaining_extent).max(child_hint); the cell keeps the largest extent from earlier layouts, so the extent never shrinks. Flutter recomputes extent from the current remaining extent on every layout.
fix_direction: Compute the non-scroll-body extent from the current remaining extent and child hint on every layout, without carrying the previous maximum forward.
limitations: Only growth of the preceding sliver was tested; shrink of the viewport and reverse axes were not. Phase change verified on a single run.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: KeepAlive does not retain a scrolled-away child
evidence: In a SliverList.builder of 40 rows, row 2 is wrapped in KeepAlive(keepAlive: true). After jumpTo(1000) Flutter keeps row 2 present; Incular drops it, as it does every other row outside the cache window. The Flutter delegate's automatic keep-alive and semantic wrappers were disabled so only the explicit KeepAlive applies.
impact: Children that must keep state while scrolled out of view (for example PageView-style content or a form that should survive scrolling) are rebuilt from scratch in Incular, losing state and re-running initialization.
cause: Incular's KeepAlive documents itself as transparent: the retained tree has no public parent-data channel, so the keep-alive request is only recorded through request() and never reaches the sliver materializer.
fix_direction: Connect KeepAlive to the sliver child manager so a kept-alive child is retained outside the cache window, as Flutter's KeepAliveParentDataMixin does.
limitations: One child at one offset was tested; toggling keepAlive off after retention and keep-alive with a SliverFixedExtentList were not. The boundary-edge flags for rows 14, 17 and 37 are the slivers-006 effect.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Resizing header reports pinned-header cache extent, building one trailing row too few
evidence: Collapse from 120 to 40 px with the default Pinned behaviour matches on header and body rects for frames 0-2. At offset 60 both sides place body rows at the same positions, but Flutter builds rows 20 and 21 and Incular does not. Flutter's resizing header reports cacheExtent calculateCacheOffset(from 0 to childExtent) = 60 at this offset; Incular's pinned_geometry reports -cacheOrigin + layoutExtent = 120, consuming twice the cache.
impact: Rows near the trailing cache edge after a resizing header are built later than in Flutter; no visible pixel difference at rest, but cache-dependent side effects and first-scroll readiness differ.
cause: ResizingHeaderRenderSliver uses pinned_geometry (the pinned persistent-header formula) for its cache. Flutter's pinned persistent header uses that formula, but Flutter's resizing header uses calculateCacheOffset over [0, childExtent]. Incular's pinned path matches Flutter's pinned path, so the difference is in the resizing header only.
fix_direction: Give the resizing header Flutter's calculateCacheOffset cache contribution over [0, child extent] rather than the pinned persistent-header formula.
limitations: The cause is inferred from the source formulas and the observed built set; no instrumentation of the consumed cache was added. Only the Pinned behaviour was compared, since Flutter has no scroll-behaviour enum.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Children whose edge exactly meets the cache boundary are built on the opposite side
evidence: Viewport 600 px, default cache 250 px, 50 px rows. At offset 0 Flutter builds rows 0-16 and Incular 0-17; row 17 starts exactly at the cache end (850). At offset 1000 Flutter builds 14-36 and Incular 15-37; row 14 ends exactly at the cache start and row 37 starts at the cache end. Built counts are equal (17 and 23), so only the edge convention differs. A non-aligned 180 px cache on fixed 40 px rows matches.
impact: Only children that touch the cache edge exactly differ in whether they are built; nothing visible differs. Relevant only where build side effects are counted.
cause: The leading and trailing cache edges are treated as half-open in opposite directions: Flutter includes the child that ends at the cache start and excludes the child that starts at the cache end, while Incular does the reverse.
fix_direction: Align the inclusive edge rule of the materialized-row range with Flutter's child range computation.
limitations: The edge rule is inferred from the built sets; the render path that produced these sets was not traced. Only 50 px rows with 250 px cache at 600 px viewports were tested.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: SliverFillRemaining has no fillOverscroll option
evidence: Flutter's SliverFillRemaining(hasScrollBody: false, fillOverscroll: true) selects RenderSliverFillRemainingAndOverscroll so the child stretches into the overscroll area of bouncing physics. Incular's SliverFillRemaining exposes only has_scroll_body; FillRemainingRenderSliver has no overscroll branch. rg for fill_overscroll and fillOverscroll finds nothing. Incular does have overscroll physics (crates/incular-scroll/src/activity.rs:275-316), so the feature is reachable.
impact: With bouncing physics a non-scrolling fill child cannot stretch to fill the overscroll gap, so a footer or empty state leaves a visible gap at the edge.
cause: The option was not ported; the non-scroll-body path always sizes to the remaining extent.
fix_direction: Add a fill_overscroll option whose layout extends the child into the overscroll area when hasScrollBody is false.
limitations: Existence and absence are established from source; no runtime twin was written because it needs a bouncing-physics overscroll drag, which the harness does not yet script for slivers.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: SliverFloatingHeader has no snapMode or snap configuration
evidence: Flutter's FloatingHeaderSnapMode (overlay or scroll) selects whether the header's layout extent follows its visible extent, and a FloatingHeaderSnapConfiguration sets the snap curve and duration. Incular's SliverFloatingHeader has only a snap bool; rg for snap_mode, SnapMode and snap_config finds no counterpart. Snap timing is fixed at the shared neutral 300 ms (slivers-002).
impact: Apps cannot choose the scroll-mode (layout-following) floating header or tune snap timing, so layout and motion differ from Flutter configurations that use them.
cause: Only the enable switch was ported; mode and configuration were not.
fix_direction: Add a snap mode with overlay and scroll variants and a snap configuration (curve and duration), with defaults matching Flutter.
limitations: Source and absence only; the mode's layout effect was not traced in a runtime twin.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md
verification_note: Verification: FloatingHeaderSnapConfiguration is Material (material/app_bar.dart:1354); the widgets-layer gap is snapMode.

title: SliverPersistentHeader has no delegate with variable extents and shrinkOffset
evidence: Flutter's SliverPersistentHeaderDelegate supplies minExtent and maxExtent and builds the child with shrinkOffset and overlapsContent. Incular's SliverPersistentHeader takes a fixed height and child only. SliverResizingHeader (sliver_descriptors.rs:1935) covers min and max extents with a child, but no delegate build receiving shrinkOffset or overlapsContent. rg for SliverPersistentHeaderDelegate and delegate in incular-widgets scrolling finds nothing.
impact: Headers whose content depends on shrinkOffset or overlapsContent cannot be expressed through SliverPersistentHeader, which is a common Flutter pattern.
cause: The delegate contract was not ported; the Incular header is fixed-extent.
fix_direction: Add a delegate contract (min extent, max extent, build with shrink offset and overlaps-content) or document SliverResizingHeader as its replacement.
limitations: Source-level API gap; SliverResizingHeader's shrink behaviour is covered by its own row and may satisfy some uses.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: No public Viewport or ShrinkWrappingViewport with anchor or center
evidence: Flutter exposes Viewport and ShrinkWrappingViewport widgets with anchor and center configuration. Incular's viewport is the internal single_sliver_viewport helper (layout.rs:2469), and CustomScrollView wraps it. rg for pub struct Viewport and anchor in incular-widgets scrolling finds no public viewport widget and no anchor option.
impact: Apps cannot build a multi-sliver viewport with an anchor or a centered origin, or a shrink-wrapped viewport, from the public API.
cause: Viewport composition is internal to the scroll view wrappers.
fix_direction: Expose a public Viewport with anchor and center, and a shrink-wrapping variant, over the existing sliver layout.
limitations: Absence is established from the public API search; whether CustomScrollView's internals support anchoring was not checked.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: SliverVisibility has no replacement sliver or maintain flags
flutter_ref: widgets/visibility.dart:356-380 (SliverVisibility: replacementSliver, maintainState, maintainAnimation, maintainSize, maintainSemantics, maintainInteractivity)
evidence: Incular SliverVisibility stores only visible and the sliver. Flutter can keep the hidden sliver's state, animation, size, semantics or interactivity, and can show a replacement sliver.
impact: Hidden slivers cannot keep their scroll extent (maintainSize) or state, so toggling visibility in a CustomScrollView shifts following slivers and discards state where Flutter can preserve them.
cause: The descriptor models only a boolean.
fix_direction: Add the replacement sliver and maintain flags with Flutter's defaults and assertions.
limitations: Source only (sweep candidate confirmed by the orchestrator).

title: Viewports have no paintOrder option
evidence: Flutter 3.41 lets a viewport paint its slivers with the first or last sliver on top; Incular has no equivalent option.
impact: Overlapping slivers (for example pinned headers over later content) cannot choose Flutter's alternative paint order.
fix_direction: Add a paint-order option to the viewport and scroll views, defaulting to Flutter's firstIsTop.
limitations: Source only; Incular's default order versus firstIsTop was not compared by pixels.
